title: Sustainable Business Models for Climate Resilience: Adapting Organisational Strategy in an Era of Environmental Uncertainty
abstract: This study investigates the application of climate-resilient sustainable business models in the manufacturing and agricultural value chains in Africa and Asia. In the context of heightened environmental volatility and regulatory scrutiny between 2020 and 2024, the study investigates adaptation strategies that are reasonably economical and ecologically viable for addressing specific regional issues. Employing a mixed-method design, quantitative analysis from 87 firms was supplemented with qualitative case studies from 12 industry leaders. The evaluation model incorporated business model innovation, resource use efficiency measurement, and adaptive capacity assessment through executive and sustainability officer interviews. Data collection was done longitudinally over 36 months, factoring in seasonal and periodic extreme weather shifts. The study identified four emergent business models with exceptional resilience: climate-responsive supply chain restructuring, community-embedded production, circular economy integration, and ecosystem service valuation. Implementing these models resulted in 28% reduced disruption costs and 17% increased resource efficiency during extreme weather events compared to traditional models across both continents. Following the comparative assessment, the study suggested adopting scenario-based planning, incorporating climate data, creating collaborative industry-wide knowledge-sharing platforms, embedding climate-related performance indicators into key figure reporting, and recalibrating governance frameworks to support strategic sustainability targets. There are contextual implementation approaches for global companies and local capital-bent firms. This research assists in understanding business model innovation in the context of climate vulnerability and competitive advantage in adapting regions. Other studies should investigate the integration of different sectors and target geographic areas more closely, focusing on enduring adaptability as organisational responses to environmental unpredictability mature.

title: The Mediating Role of Maladaptive Coping in the Association Between Neuroticism and Family Accommodation in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
abstract: Objective Family accommodation, in which relatives facilitate obsessive-compulsive symptoms, is highly prevalent in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and associated with poor treatment outcomes. Although neuroticism and maladaptive coping have been linked to OCD severity, the mechanisms by which personality traits relate to family accommodation remain poorly understood. This study examined associations between neuroticism, coping strategies, symptom severity, and family accommodation in OCD, and tested whether maladaptive coping mediates the neuroticism–family accommodation association.Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study with 149 adults diagnosed with OCD via the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5 at a university hospital outpatient clinic. Participants completed the Family Accommodation Scale–Patient Version, Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale Self-Report, Big Five Inventory-44, and Brief COPE. Hierarchical regression and bootstrap-based mediation analyses (PROCESS Model 4; 5,000 bootstrap samples) were performed, controlling for age, sex, education, and symptom severity.Results OCD symptom severity (β=0.342, p<0.001) and maladaptive coping (β=0.347, p<0.001) were significantly associated with family accommodation, explaining 26.6% of its variance. Neuroticism was not directly associated with family accommodation; however, mediation analysis revealed a significant indirect association through maladaptive coping (B=0.189, 95% confidence interval [0.034 to 0.399]).Conclusion These cross-sectional findings suggest that maladaptive coping may represent a potential behavioral pathway linking neuroticism to family accommodation in OCD. While the findings provide a theoretical rationale for further investigating coping mechanisms, longitudinal and experimental studies are needed to determine whether interventions targeting maladaptive coping lead to reductions in family accommodation.

title: The Interplay of Digital Literacy and Parenting Styles on Critical Thinking: The Mediating Role of Emotional Intelligence in Islamic Education
abstract: Understanding how digital competencies and family environments relate to students’ emotional and cognitive development can inform Islamic Religious Education (Pendidikan Agama Islam; PAI). This study examined the relationships of digital literacy and parenting styles with students’ emotional intelligence and critical thinking skills, including the mediating role of emotional intelligence. A quantitative design was employed involving 79 students selected from a population of 377 at MAN 1 Mojokerto through proportionate stratified random sampling. Data were collected using validated and reliable questionnaires and analyzed through path analysis following statistical assumption testing. The findings indicated that digital literacy and authoritative parenting were positively and significantly associated with both emotional intelligence and critical thinking skills. Authoritarian and permissive parenting showed comparatively limited associations with these outcomes. Emotional intelligence also emerged as a significant statistical mediator linking digital literacy and parenting styles to critical thinking. These findings suggest that emotional intelligence provides a relevant link between students’ digital and family contexts and their critical thinking in PAI, although the reported relationships do not establish causality. The study contributes an integrated account of these relationships within Islamic religious education and highlights the relevance of digital literacy development, supportive parenting, and emotional learning to educational efforts aimed at strengthening students’ critical thinking.

title: Prevalence of multi-nuclear and multi-ovular follicles within paediatric ovarian tissue: recommendations for systematic subclassification
abstract: Abstract STUDY QUESTION Do premenarcheal girls have a high proportion of morphologically abnormal ovarian follicles? SUMMARY ANSWER A higher prevalence of follicles with an abnormal number of oocytes and nuclei was found in premenarcheal ovarian tissue compared with postmenarcheal tissue. WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY Morphological aberrations of ovarian follicles, including multi-nuclear oocytes and multi-ovular follicles, have been documented across species, including humans. These specific morphological aberrations, together with other types of abnormal follicles, are more prevalent in the ovaries of children and decline in number with age. However, detailed studies of the prevalence of multi-nuclear and multi-ovular follicles in paediatric ovarian tissue are limited. STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION This was an observational study of the ovaries of children and adolescents who underwent ovarian cryopreservation prior to chemotherapy. PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS The study recruited participants aged 0–18 years who underwent ovarian tissue cryopreservation at a single centre. Haematoxylin and eosin-stained slides of ovarian biopsies were scanned and analysed to determine follicle number and aberrations in morphology and the cortical area was measured. Abnormal follicles were defined as those with an abnormal number of oocytes or oocyte nuclei. Relationships with menarcheal status (premenarcheal; postmenarcheal) and age were assessed. MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE A total of 149 participants’ ovarian samples were evaluated in the study, of whom 67 (45%) had follicles with abnormal numbers of oocytes or oocyte nuclei. Amongst 117 participants who had adequate follicle numbers, these abnormal follicle types accounted for 3.8% (902/23 891) of the total number of follicles and were significantly more common in premenarcheal girls (52/80; 65.0%) compared with postmenarcheal girls (15/37; 40.5%; P = 0.013). Ovular abnormalities (in 76.7% of abnormal follicles) were more common than nuclear abnormalities (in 23.3% of abnormal follicles; P < 0.001). Bi-ovular primordial follicles were the most common abnormality, comprising 54% of the total abnormal follicle population and were present in 41.9% of participants. LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION Small ovarian biopsies were analysed, which may not fully represent the whole ovary. There is also a limited number of participants in each menarcheal group. WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS Our study highlights that although follicle numbers are high in the prepubertal ovary, there was also a high proportion of follicles containing abnormal numbers of oocytes and oocyte nuclei. Further longitudinal and functional studies are recommended to determine whether this impacts fertility and the longevity of function following ovarian tissue grafting for restoration of fertility in these participants. Our work supports a separate multioocytic follicle class within the NICHD follicle classification, and we suggest expanding it to include a distinct multinuclear follicle category (oocyte contains more than one nucleus), as these likely represent different aberrations in oogenesis or folliculogenesis. This classification with clear definitions and nomenclature may improve consistency in reporting and facilitate future research. FUNDING This work was supported by an MRFF Grant (MRFAR000308) supporting the funding of coauthors M.J. and M.A. Y.J. is supported through a Dame Kate Campbell Fellowship, The University of Melbourne. Co-authors V.G.-L. and J.Y.M. are supported through National Institute of Health (NIH) Z1A HD009005. DISCLOSURES No conflict of interests are declared. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER n/a.

title: “It Felt Like We Were a Council of Elders”: Black Teacher-Coaches Sustaining Professional Identity with Affinity, Support, and Communal Care
abstract: Abstract This study examines how Black teacher-coaches (BTCs) build and sustain professional and pedagogical networks of support amid divisive concepts legislation that restricts classroom discussions related to race, identity, inequality, and systemic oppression. Drawing upon frameworks of communalism, collective Black identity, and Black historical consciousness, this research investigates how three BTCs collectively responded to legislative pressures that seek to constrain instructional autonomy and limit engagement with Black intellectual traditions. Findings demonstrate that these educators tended to each other with communal efforts that mirrored the purpose and functionality of a Black affinity group. Collectively, the participants supported one another’s beliefs and practices through mutual care, demonstrating what it meant to learn from their respective communities, and how their shared identities as Black educators and athletic coaches shaped their bond. This study contributes to scholarship by highlighting how communal educational practices function as mechanisms of support and resilience under restrictive legislative conditions.

title: Targeting Olfaction for Control: OR17 and Its Ligand E-β-Caryophyllene Contribute to Host Location in Phthorimaea Absoluta
journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
abstract: Abstract Odorant receptors (ORs) of phytophagous insects mediate detection and discrimination of plant volatiles for host location and oviposition. Using the reverse chemical ecology approach, we identified host-related odorants and receptors in Phthorimaea absoluta. Molecular docking identified limonene, α-terpinene, and E-β-caryophyllene as putative ligands of OR9, OR6, and OR17, respectively. All three compounds elicited significant antennal responses in both sexes, with stronger responses in females. In Y-tube assays, E-β-caryophyllene attracted females, and a ternary blend (5:3:2) elicited significantly greater attraction than individual compounds. This female-biased attraction persisted across 72 h cage assays and for at least 18 days in a greenhouse. PabsOR17 silencing significantly reduced female behavioral responses to E-β-caryophyllene. These findings support the contribution of OR17-mediated E-β-caryophyllene detection to female host location, providing a potential molecular target for female-oriented behavioral disruption and a reverse chemical ecology framework for semiochemical-based pest management.
